=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached singly at different nodes along the stem, alternating sides)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced out along the stem with distinct internodes, not clustered together)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade attached to the stem, not divided into leaflets)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): toothed (margin shows distinct, small, regular teeth along the edges)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaf is widest near the middle and tapers towards both ends)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tapers to a distinct, elongated point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base of the leaf appears broadly curved without a distinct taper)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with secondary veins branching off to the sides)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, closely spaced, and numerous (runs parallel to the margin)
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, rugose (surface is glossy and has a textured, slightly bumpy appearance due to prominent venation)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (surface appears smooth and lacks visible hairs)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is noticeably shorter than the leaf blade)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole appears round in cross-section and smooth)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears green, slender, and flexible, characteristic of a young seedling)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    19.	Stem color: green (appears green, similar to the leaf color)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no visible ridges or lenticels on the visible stem parts)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the leaf base)
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible)
F. Notes: The leaf margin is consistently serrulate (finely toothed) across all images. The rugose texture is a prominent feature of the leaf surface. The plant is growing on the forest floor amongst leaf litter and other small seedlings.
